column1: # THE PARITY LEDGER -- known TypeScript/Go divergences. THIS FILE SHOULD
# NORMALLY BE EMPTY OF ROWS.
# test/spec/*.tsv is the contract: a row lives there only once BOTH
# implementations satisfy it. This file is the debt register for the
# opposite case -- a behaviour where the two ports are known to DISAGREE,
# recorded so the disagreement is visible and tracked instead of being
# rediscovered, and so nobody baselines one engine's output as the shared
# contract by accident.
# It is deliberately a .tsv living beside the suite, so it is read
# whenever the spec is read. Both runners (ts/test/spec.test.ts and
# go/spec_test.go) glob test/spec/*.tsv and skip comment and blank lines,
# so a file of comments contributes zero rows and asserts nothing.
# HOW TO USE IT
# A divergence is a BUG, not a feature. The default response is to fix
# the engine, not to write here. Add an entry ONLY when the divergence
# cannot be fixed from this repository right now -- e.g. it originates in
# a pinned @tabnas dependency, or the correct behaviour is an open
# language-design question.
# An entry MUST carry:
#   1. an issue reference (the tracking issue for the fix), and
#   2. a reason it is not simply fixed, and
#   3. the exact divergent inputs and BOTH engines' outputs.
# An entry is removed -- not amended -- when the divergence is fixed, and
# the behaviour then earns real rows in the appropriate spec file.
# Entries carry NO data rows: a row here would be executed by both
# runners and, by definition, could not pass in both. Everything below is
# commentary.
# NOTE (2026-08-11): five entries were RECLASSIFIED from DIVERGENCE.md
# by maintainer decision -- previously accepted as permanent, now debt
# to be fixed; only the Unicode table vintage remains there. Three are
# already fixed and removed (#29 message text, #30 parse-level canon,
# #31 invalid-source stages); the surrogate (#24) and malformed-input
# (#32) entries below remain, blocked on upstream @tabnas work and a
# direction decision.
# OPEN -- lone surrogates in quoted strings folded to U+FFFD by Go.
#   issue: #24 (REOPENED 2026-08-11; the 2026-08-11 decision to accept
#   this permanently is reversed -- parity is required). Go conflates
#   values TS keeps distinct, breaking the lattice law that two
#   different values never unify; as map keys it silently merges
#   distinct entries.
#   Divergent input:  x:"\ud800" x:"�"
#   TypeScript: error, Cannot unify values at $.x (values distinct)
#   Go:         SUCCESS, {"x":"�"} (values conflated)
#   Not simply fixed because the fold happens at LEX time in the
#   pinned @tabnas/parser Go lexer (deliberate upstream, matching
#   encoding/json), and the direction is undecided: refuse unpaired
#   surrogates in BOTH ports (restores the law, removes a working TS
#   capability) or preserve in both (upstream lexer change + Go
#   emission path). The upstream per-port pinning tests assert
#   OPPOSITE results on purpose and must flip together with the fix.
#   Paired forms all agree and keep their real rows (scalar.tsv
#   surrogate-*).
# OPEN -- malformed-input acceptance edges and invalid-UTF-8
#   replacement counts.
#   issue: #32. Degenerate inputs where one parser errors and the
#   other produces differently-shaped junk; and invalid UTF-8 where
#   the ports emit a different NUMBER of U+FFFD replacements.
#   Divergent inputs:  pref(1-3)   close(([]%))   1'00]...   "q k""?:...
#     (acceptance: one side errors, the other parses to junk)
#   And the byte sequence E2 82 (truncated three-byte UTF-8) inside a
#   string:
#   TypeScript: ONE U+FFFD (Node replaces at file decode)
#   Go:         TWO U+FFFD (raw bytes carried to the encoder)
#   Not simply fixed because the acceptance split is largely upstream
#   in the @tabnas stack, and the src column cannot carry raw invalid
#   bytes -- fixes pin via per-port twin tests over byte fixtures.
#   Well-formed sources are unaffected throughout.
# OPEN -- a cycle routed through a function errors with different
#   codes. issue: #35. `a:$.b b:upper($.a)` errors in BOTH engines
#   (verdict agrees) but TS reports `internal` -- a caught stack
#   overflow, its documented no-depth-guard fallback -- where Go
#   proves `path_cycle`.
#   Divergent input:  a:$.b b:upper($.a)
#   TypeScript: error code internal (RangeError caught; threshold
#     environment-dependent, classification deterministic)
#   Go:         error code path_cycle
#   Not simply fixed because the correct answer (path_cycle) requires
#   TS to PROVE the cycle -- chase detection through function
#   arguments, or an explicit depth budget that classifies as
#   path_cycle -- an engine change on the TS side tracked by #35; Go
#   already reports the proof. No errc row may pin either code
#   meanwhile.
# CLOSED -- lone surrogates in quoted strings folded to U+FFFD by Go.
#   issue: #24. Two separate things lived under this entry; both are
#   settled, in opposite ways, and the difference is the point.
#   The BRACED-SPELLING half was a plain upstream BUG. The pair lookahead
#   in @tabnas/parser's Go lexer sat inside the 4-hex escape branch and
#   recognised only its own spelling, while the braced branch wrote its
#   rune immediately with no lookahead at all -- so `\u{d83d}\u{de00}`,
#   and both MIXED spellings, decoded to two U+FFFD. Go REJECTED documents
#   TypeScript accepted, the opposite direction from the rest of #24.
#   Fixed in @tabnas/parser 0.8.4 by pairing on the decoded code unit
#   sequence rather than per escape spelling, and it now has real rows
#   (scalar.tsv `surrogate-*`), which is where a resolved behaviour goes.
#   The LONE-SURROGATE half was never a bug upstream -- it is deliberate
#   there -- and the question was whether aontu should refuse an unpaired
#   surrogate in BOTH ports to restore the lattice law. DECLINED
#   (2026-08-11 morning): a documented divergence was judged the smaller
#   cost, and the entry left this file as ACCEPTED, recorded in
#   DIVERGENCE.md.
#   REVERSED the same day: by maintainer decision the divergence is not
#   acceptable and must be fixed. #24 is reopened and the case is OPEN
#   again -- see its live entry ABOVE, which supersedes this note. This
#   closed entry stays only for the braced-spelling half's history.
# The other entry this file has carried is CLOSED; what it recorded is
# kept below, because how it was closed is the part worth remembering.
# CLOSED -- integer-kind values above 2^53 that need more than 17
#   significant digits to write exactly. issue: #21.
#   TypeScript held an integer-kind peg as a JS number and rendered it
#   with Number.toString, which emits the SHORTEST decimal that parses
#   back to the same double. Go held it as an int64 and printed the true
#   value. So 2^60 was `1152921504606847000` in one port and
#   `1152921504606846976` in the other -- two different integers that
#   happen to round to the same double.
#   The entry twice recorded a resolution that turned out to be wrong:
#   that the number tower's D7 (a lossy integer literal is refused)
#   would remove the divergence by refusing the inputs. It does not. D7
#   refuses a literal binary64 cannot carry EXACTLY; it does not refuse
#   one that is merely large, and every value in this window (2^60,
#   2^63-1024) is exactly representable. THE RULE IS EXACTNESS, NOT
#   MAGNITUDE -- the same misreading, in three separate places, that the
#   Phase 6 spec rows had to correct for the hex literals.
#   That mistake is the reason this note survives the entry. A ledger
#   entry closed against a plausible-sounding phase that does not
#   actually touch it looks exactly like a closed entry, and the only
#   thing that caught it both times was re-probing BOTH CLIs at the
#   exact inputs written down here -- which is why rule 3 above demands
#   they be written down.
#   What actually closed it: once D7 landed, every remaining divergent
#   case was one where BOTH ports held exactly the value the source
#   asked for, so "agreeing on the text would only agree on a wrong
#   number" stopped being true. There was a right answer, and Go already
#   printed it. TypeScript now renders an integer-kind value by its
#   exact digits in BOTH places -- IntegerVal.canon, and generate(),
#   which past Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER hands back a `bigint` so the
#   exact-JSON emitter can write the digits (JSON.stringify of the JS
#   number reproduces the very 17-digit form canon had just dropped, so
#   the emitter had to be part of the fix). The window is pinned by real
#   rows now: number-tower.tsv, `EXACT INTEGER RENDERING` for canon and
#   `gens-exact-int-*` for the bytes, both routes in -- literal and
#   exact sum.
# NOT recorded here, because they are already documented as deliberate,
# permanent non-parity in AGENTS.md ("Known TS/Go divergences"): error
# MESSAGE text, parse-level (non-unify) canon, the canon of sources that
# are invalid in both ports, and the malformed-input acceptance edges.
# Only the substring an err-mode spec row asserts is contractual.
# Also not a divergence, though it is a difference: the NATIVE TYPE an
# integer generates as. Go returns an int64 at every magnitude;
# TypeScript returns a `number` up to Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER and a
# `bigint` above it, because its leaf is a double and a double past that
# line no longer renders its own digits. The serialised BYTES agree --
# that is what the gens rows pin -- and the difference is forced by the
# storage, not chosen. It is pinned per-port instead: ts/test/
# exactjson.test.ts and go/generate_test.go.
